news.headline: AMD Q1 2026 Blowout: Revenue $10.3B, Data Center +57% YoY; Stock Hits All-Time High
news.body: AMD reported Q1 2026 revenue of $10.3B, beating the $9.85B consensus estimate by 4%, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.37 vs. $1.29 expected — a 43% year-over-year jump. Data center revenue surged 57% to $5.8B, driven by EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPU shipments, with Meta already committed to deploying 6GW of AMD Instinct GPUs. Q2 guidance of $11.2B revenue topped Street expectations of ~$10.5B, implying 46% year-over-year growth. The stock hit an all-time high of $379.90 in after-hours trading, up roughly 8-15% depending on the session reference point, cementing AMD as the primary Nvidia challenger in AI infrastructure.

news.headline: Pinterest Surges 15% on Q2 Guidance Beat; Duolingo Drops ~10% Despite EPS Beat
news.body: Pinterest shares popped 15% after reporting Q2 revenue guidance of $1.13B–$1.15B, topping the $1.11B analyst estimate, triggering a major short squeeze given the stock's 15.4% short float. Conversely, Duolingo fell roughly 10% in Tuesday trading despite beating Q1 EPS ($0.89 vs. $0.76 expected) and revenue ($292M vs. $289M), as investors focused on a narrowed 2026 bookings growth guide of ~10.5% and the CFO's comment that strategic AI product investments would push returns to 2027 and beyond. Daily active users grew 21% to 56.5M but slower monetization conversion weighed on sentiment. The divergence highlights how forward guidance — not backward beats — is driving sharp post-earnings moves in consumer tech.

news.headline: Micron Gains 5% as AI Demand Confirms HBM Sold Out Through 2026; Street-High $1,000 PT Set
news.body: Micron Technology (MU) rose ~5% on May 5 as bullish analyst commentary and AI infrastructure demand catalysts reinforced the stock's AI memory thesis. DA Davidson initiated coverage with a Street-high $1,000 price target while TD Cowen raised its target to $660 from $550, both citing Micron's 2026 HBM capacity being fully sold out under binding contracts. Hyperscaler earnings (Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) confirmed memory costs are a primary AI buildout driver, providing direct revenue visibility for Micron. With Q2 FY2026 revenue already reported at $23.9B (+196% YoY) and EPS of $12.20 vs. $9.21 expected, Micron has become a consensus core AI infrastructure holding.

news.headline: Amazon Launches Supply Chain Services; UPS Drops 10.5%, FedEx Falls 9.1%
news.body: Amazon officially launched 'Amazon Supply Chain Services' on May 4, opening its entire logistics stack — freight, warehousing, inventory management, fulfillment, and parcel delivery — to third-party enterprises including P&G, 3M, and American Eagle Outfitters. UPS plunged 10.47% to $96.31, its largest single-session decline in years, while FedEx fell 9.1% in its worst day in more than a year; GXO Logistics and Forward Air suffered double-digit declines. The move is particularly damaging for UPS, which was already strategically cutting Amazon volumes by 50% and pivoting to higher-margin SMB and healthcare clients — the exact segment Amazon is now targeting. Baird analysts warned of near-term weakness across the broader freight and air cargo complex.

news.headline: GameStop's Unsolicited $56B eBay Bid Sinks GME 10%, Lifts EBAY 5%
news.body: GameStop announced an unsolicited, nonbinding proposal to acquire eBay for $125 per share (50% cash, 50% stock), valuing the e-commerce platform at ~$55.5B — roughly 4.7x GameStop's own ~$12B market cap. CEO Ryan Cohen secured a non-binding $20B financing letter from TD Bank but analysts and prominent investor Michael Burry — who subsequently sold his GME stake — flagged the deal's estimated 7.7x debt-to-EBITDA leverage as near-distressed territory. GameStop shares fell 10% on Monday while eBay gained ~5%, trading well below the $125 offer price, signaling deep market skepticism over deal closure. eBay's board confirmed receipt and said it would 'carefully review' the proposal, with no prior discussions having taken place.

news.headline: Nikkei 225 Reopens Post-Golden Week With BoJ Hawkish Risk and Yen Surge in Focus
news.body: Japan's Tokyo Stock Exchange reopened on May 6, 2026 after being closed since May 1 for Golden Week holidays, with the Nikkei 225 last closing at 59,513 — a gain of 0.38% on its final pre-holiday session. Investors returned to markets pricing in a yen that had surged more than 1% against the dollar to 156.15 during the break, widely attributed to Bank of Japan intervention, which typically weighs on Japan's export-heavy stocks. The BoJ also revised its FY2026 inflation forecast sharply higher to 2.8% from 1.9% while halving its growth forecast to 0.5%, raising the prospect of further rate hikes. Tech leaders Tokyo Electron (+6.9%) and SoftBank Group (+3.9%) had led the final pre-holiday session, but investors must now reckon with the combined headwinds of a stronger yen and a more hawkish policy board.

news.headline: Samsung Hits $1 Trillion Market Cap, KOSPI Clears 7,000 for First Time
news.body: Samsung Electronics surged ~14% on May 6 in Seoul, pushing its market capitalisation to ₩1,500 trillion ($1.03 trillion) — making it only the second Asian company after TSMC to breach the $1 trillion mark. The rally was fuelled by blowout Q1 2026 results (operating profit up more than 8x YoY to ₩57.2 trillion, record revenue of ₩133.9 trillion) and booming AI-driven demand for HBM and DRAM. The KOSPI closed at a record 7,384.56, up 6.45%, breaching 7,000 for the first time as foreign and institutional investors drove heavy inflows.

news.headline: Taiwan TAIEX Sets Back-to-Back Records; MediaTek Hits Limit-Up, Foxconn +5%
news.body: Taiwan's TAIEX closed at a fresh all-time high of 40,769.29 on May 5, the second consecutive record after first crossing 40,000 on May 4, with turnover near NT$998 billion. MediaTek hit its daily price limit at NT$3,155 for the second straight session, setting a new record high, while Foxconn rose 5.27% on AI server demand. TSMC dipped slightly but broader tech and traditional industrials advanced, reinforcing Taiwan's position as the world's 7th-largest market by capitalisation.

news.headline: China CSI 300 Gains 1.6% on Labor Day Return; Hang Seng Tech +1.1%
news.body: China's CSI 300 added 1.62% on May 5 as mainland markets reopened after the Labor Day holiday break, with technology and consumer names leading gains alongside renewed global AI optimism. Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 0.62% and the Hang Seng Tech index climbed 1.05%, tracking Wall Street's record close driven by AMD's strong guidance and Intel's AI-related surge. The broader Asia MSCI gauge climbed 1% to a fresh all-time record, with oil prices easing after Trump paused 'Project Freedom' in the Strait of Hormuz, reducing a key risk factor for energy-importing Asian equities.

news.headline: SK Hynix Surges 12.5% to Join Samsung Above ₩1,000 Trillion Market Cap
news.body: SK Hynix jumped 12.52% on May 4 to close at ₩1.447 million per share, pushing its market cap past ₩1,031 trillion (~$697 billion) — only the second Korean-listed company to cross that threshold after Samsung Electronics. The move was driven by Q1 2026 record revenue of ₩52.6 trillion (up 198% YoY) on insatiable AI memory demand, and by $2.1 billion in net foreign buying on the day. The KOSPI itself surged 5.12% to a record 6,936.99, with Korea Exchange data showing the second-highest ever single-session foreign net buying since October 2025.

news.headline: WTI Surges ~3% as US-Iran Exchange Fire in Strait of Hormuz; Fujairah Terminal Hit
news.body: WTI crude futures surged roughly 3% to $105/bbl on Monday after US forces repelled Iranian attacks while escorting two US-flagged vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's IRGC launching cruise missiles at American warships and commercial vessels. The UAE confirmed a fire at its Fujairah oil terminal following an Iranian drone strike, marking one of the first major infrastructure hits in weeks; a tanker was also struck by drones near the strait. By Tuesday WTI pulled back slightly below $104 but held most of the rally, as markets assessed whether the four-week ceasefire remained viable. The flare-up reinforces expectations that the Hormuz route will remain closed until a formal US-Iran agreement is reached, sustaining a multi-million bpd supply shortfall.

news.headline: Gold Drops ~2% to $4,540 as Hormuz Escalation Fans Rate-Hike Fears
news.body: Gold fell to $4,540/oz on Monday — its lowest since late March — and recovered only partially to ~$4,550 on Tuesday, as renewed US-Iran hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz drove oil prices higher and amplified global inflation concerns. Iran's Fars news agency reported two missiles struck a US Navy frigate near Jask Island, while the IRGC released a map designating areas of the strait under Iranian military control. The conflict, now in its tenth week, has pushed gold down roughly 13–15% from its January all-time high of ~$5,595, as surging energy costs raise fears central banks may hold or raise rates — eroding gold's appeal versus yield-bearing assets. World Gold Council Q1 2026 data showed central banks boosted reserves, providing a structural floor, but oil-driven inflation headwinds dominate near-term sentiment.

news.headline: UAE Formally Exits OPEC on May 1, Removing ~12% of Cartel Output Capacity
news.body: The UAE's withdrawal from OPEC took effect May 1, ending a 59-year membership and removing the cartel's third-largest producer — roughly 12% of OPEC capacity and ~3% of global supply at ~3.4 million bpd. Crude prices initially dipped on supply-glut fears before rebounding above $105 WTI and $112 Brent as Iran-related risk premiums dominated; longer-dated contracts are pricing in a looser 2027 market if Abu Dhabi hits its 5 million bpd capacity target. The exit, triggered by frustration over quota constraints versus ADNOC's 4.85 million bpd capacity, has heightened fragmentation risk within OPEC+, with analysts flagging Kazakhstan and Nigeria as potential next departures. Wood Mackenzie estimates the move is "the biggest schism in OPEC since it was founded in 1960," with medium-term price war risk rising if UAE-Saudi competition for market share intensifies.

news.headline: Global LNG Gap Widens: TTF +35%, JKM +51% Since Hormuz Closure; Qatar Offline
news.body: European TTF LNG futures held near $14.80/MMBtu for the week ending April 24 — up 35% since the February 28 Hormuz closure — while the Asia-Pacific JKM benchmark surged 51% to $16.02/MMBtu, per EIA data. The closure has stranded approximately 20% of global LNG supply, with QatarEnergy's force majeure on Ras Laffan exports still in effect; the IEA warns damage to Qatar's liquefaction infrastructure could delay the global LNG supply wave by at least two years and cost ~120 bcm of supply through 2030. US Henry Hub prices have diverged sharply lower (-9% since February) as domestic terminals operate at 94% capacity with limited ability to offset global shortfalls. European storage ended winter at just 28% full versus a 41% five-year average, keeping refill-season buying pressure acute.

news.headline: US Wheat Hits Near Two-Year High at $6.53/Bu on Great Plains Drought; India Resumes Exports
news.body: Wheat futures spiked to $6.53/bu on April 28 — the highest since June 2024 — driven by severe drought across the US Great Plains, with roughly 90% of Nebraska and Oklahoma affected and USDA winter wheat ratings at just 30% good-to-excellent, the weakest for this time of year since 2023. By May 5–6 prices retreated to ~$6.13/bu as rainfall forecasts offered partial relief to dry western Plains regions, but markets remain on edge ahead of the USDA crop progress update. Separately, India resumed wheat exports for the first time in four years, leveraging ample domestic stocks and elevated global prices to capitalize on the supply gap. Fertilizer cost-push pressures from the Middle East conflict are compounding crop production costs globally, with EU corn acreage in France potentially down 15% as farmers cut input use.
